llm.reply:
The trials retrieved for this query are all thyroid cancer studies, not trials enrolling carcinoma not otherwise specified as a defined entity [1]. They span radioimmunotherapy with transplant, thalidomide, irinotecan, tanespimycin, and suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid [5]. None of the trial titles mentions carcinoma not otherwise specified, so they only partly match the question [4].

## Retrieved Thyroid Trials

The first trial is Radioimmunotherapy With or Without Chemotherapy Plus Peripheral Stem Cell Transplantation in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer [1]. The second is Thalidomide in Treating Patients With Thyroid Cancer [2]. The third is Irinotecan in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Inoperable Thyroid Cancer [3]. The fourth is Tanespimycin in Treating Patients With Inoperable Locoregionally Advanced or Metastatic Thyroid Cancer [4]. The fifth is Suberoylanilide Hydroxamic Acid in Treating Patients With Metastatic and/or Locally Advanced or Locally Recurrent Thyroid Cancer [5].

## Related NOS Records

One related MedGen concept is Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [7]. In the literature, NOS carcinoma appears as a breast cancer morphology category in PMID 15365566 [8]. That study reported the lowest survival for this group among microscopically confirmed categories [9: "ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma to 95% (95% CI 90-100) for special types"]. It also found that tumour type predicts survival [9: "Morphology and hormone receptor status were confirmed as significant survival predictors"].

The retrieved trials all concern thyroid cancer, and none names carcinoma not otherwise specified as its condition, so they only partly answer the question. ## Retrieved Thyroid Trials

A third trial is Irinotecan in Treating Patients With Metastatic or Inoperable Thyroid Cancer [3]. A fourth is Tanespimycin in Treating Patients With Inoperable Locoregionally Advanced or Metastatic Thyroid Cancer [4]. A fifth is Suberoylanilide Hydroxamic Acid in Treating Patients With Metastatic and/or Locally Advanced or Locally Recurrent Thyroid Cancer [5].

## Related MedGen Concept

The closest disease record retrieved is Medullary Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified [7].

## Literature on NOS Carcinoma

The main related paper is Prognostic value of morphology and hormone receptor status in breast cancer - a population-based study. [6]. Its PubMed identifier is 15365566 [8]. In European registry breast cancer cases, NOS carcinoma had the lowest five-year relative survival among histologically confirmed types [9: "ranged from 66% (95% CI 61-71) for NOS carcinoma to 95% (95% CI 90-100) for special types"]. Tumour morphology remained prognostic after adjustment [9: "Morphology and hormone receptor status were confirmed as significant survival predictors in this population-based study, even after adjusting for age and stage at diagnosis"].
